chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth."

He said: He shows them the metamorphosis (al-masakh) in their own selves, and He shows them the breakdown/collapse of the horizons upon them, so they see the Power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in their selves and in the horizons.
I said to him: [What is meant by] 'until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth'?
He said: The emergence of Al-Qa'im is the truth from the Presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which the creatures will see; it is inevitable.

key_terms.الآفَاق: Horizons or regions of the sky/earth
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: The Truth (referring to the emergence of the Imam)
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Awakened One, a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.الْمَسْخ: Metamorphosis or transformation of physical form

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'signs in the horizons and in their souls' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates Quran 41:53 by distinguishing between internal signs of metamorphosis (al-masakh) and external cosmic upheavals, both serving to manifest divine power. He specifically links the phrase 'until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth' to the inevitable emergence of Al-Qa'im, framing his reappearance as the ultimate, undeniable proof of divine truth witnessed by all creation. This interpretation underscores the eschatological significance of the Mahdi in Shia theology as the culmination of divine signs.
